children: Uber Technologies (UBER) is drawing attention after President and Chief Operating Officer Andrew Macdonald bought 70,000 shares, putting about $5.3 million into the ride-hailing company, according to a Sept. 8 regulatory filing.
The purchases were completed Sept. 4 through two transactions. Macdonald acquired 54,325 shares at a weighted average of $75.6526 and another 15,675 shares at $76.4425.
The filing shows the actual purchase prices varied within each transaction. The first group changed hands between $75.23 and $76.22, while the second covered prices from $76.23 to $76.85.
Following the transactions, Macdonald directly owned 426,320 Uber shares. The executive serves as the company's president and chief operating officer, according to the filing.

Uber last reported second-quarter adjusted earnings per share of 81 cents, beating the consensus estimate by one cent. Revenue reached $14.19 billion, up 12.17% from a year earlier but below expectations by about $74.8 million.
The insider purchase gives investors a fresh data point as they assess Uber's valuation and operating outlook.

title: Uber Stock Gets Insider Vote as President Buys 70,000 Shares
